chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Known to musicians but not writers: a conspiracy?
summary: Willard and Collins agree all musicians know him, yet critics ignore him; Willard has known his work for twenty years.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: You are obviously well known among the musicians, but why --
Well, that's what they're writing about, musicians. They're not writing about doctors.
But I mean, you're only being ignored by the critics or writers. I don't think the public --
But all the musicians know you.
And want you to work with them.
Well, by the same token I think the writers should know me then.
I think they should too and I don't understand it either. I don't know the explanation why you're not represented in those books.
I just don't understand it, whether it's a conspiracy or what. Did they get together and say look, John Collins does not exist, you know, he does not play guitar. You know.
It almost makes you believe that.
I'm telling you it's just amazing. But any way, you know that I do exist.
Yes, I've been aware for more than 20 years.
